title: Define GA success metrics + readiness criteria for Private backup/restore toolkit
creator: Vivek Kulkarni
description:
## Context
We are preparing to take the Redwood Private backup/restore + DR toolkit to GA for VPC and on-prem (including partially/fully air-gapped). Engineering deliverables are tracking well, but we are missing crisp, measurable GA success metrics and a single readiness checklist that Engineering/SRE/Security/Docs/SE can use for launch decisions and pilot exit.

This issue defines:
1) GA success metrics (product + operational)
2) Packaging readiness criteria (installer/CLI + Helm + Terraform + air-gapped)
3) Documentation readiness criteria (operator-facing + support/SRE-facing)
4) Pilot exit criteria and GA sign-off process

Non-goals:
- Defining a managed DR service offering (this remains tooling + documentation for customer operators + SE/SRE assistance).

## Proposed GA definition (what GA means)
GA for Private backup/restore means:
- A customer operator (with standard Kubernetes + cloud/on-prem permissions) can run backup create/verify and restore (in-place + to-new-cluster) using documented procedures.
- The system emits sufficient observability (metrics + logs + dashboards + alerts) to support oncall and to prove backup freshness.
- Security posture is review-ready (encryption + key handling + least privilege guidance + evidence capture) for regulated enterprise reviews.

## GA success metrics (targets)
### A) Backup success + freshness (per cluster)
1) Scheduled backup success rate: 
- Target: >= 99.0% successful scheduled backups per cluster measured weekly (success = backup job completed and verification passed).
- Guardrail: <= 1 consecutive missed backup window before alerting escalates from warning to page (with suppression options for paused clusters).

2) Backup age SLO:
- Standard tier: last successful backup age <= 24h (95% of time).
- Strict tier: last successful backup age <= 6h (95% of time) for customers configured for higher frequency.

3) Backup integrity:
- Target: 100% of GA-eligible backups include checksums + manifest, and `backup verify` detects corruption/partial upload in testing (i.e., verification fails when expected).

### B) Operator time (time-to-safe-backup / time-to-restore)
We need metrics that align to customer pain: operator time and end-to-end time. We will track both.

Definitions:
- Operator time = hands-on keyboard time following runbook (excluding waiting on long-running jobs).
- End-to-end time = wall-clock from starting procedure to passing final validation gate.

Targets (for reference environments; see “Measurement plan”):
1) Backup create + verify:
- Operator time: <= 20 minutes (standard tier)
- End-to-end: <= 60 minutes for typical control-plane DB + artifacts (assumes baseline throughput to storage)

2) In-place restore (control plane DB restore + artifacts + restart order + smoke tests):
- Operator time: <= 60 minutes
- End-to-end RTO: <= 4 hours in standard tier reference env

3) Restore to new cluster (bootstrap + restore + cutover checklist):
- Operator time: <= 2 hours
- End-to-end RTO: <= 8 hours in standard tier reference env

Notes:
- These are GA targets, not contractual SLAs. We should publish them as guidance ranges and make constraints explicit (storage bandwidth, artifact size, DB size, k8s health).

### C) Restore drill outcomes (game day readiness)
1) Restore drill pass rate:
- Target: >= 90% pass rate across GA acceptance drills (internal) using the current runbooks (pass = restore completed + validation gates passed without undocumented steps).

2) Repeatability:
- Target: at least 2 distinct scenarios completed end-to-end in game day format with evidence captured:
  - Scenario 1: lost control plane Postgres (PITR path where supported)
  - Scenario 2: new-cluster restore + cutover

3) RPO attainment:
- Standard tier: RPO <= 24h demonstrated in drill evidence
- Strict tier: RPO <= 6h demonstrated for at least one drill env

### D) Supportability + incident reduction
1) Runbook-driven resolution:
- Target: Support/SRE can follow troubleshooting runbook to root cause in <= 30 minutes for top 3 failure modes (AccessDenied, throttling/timeout, DB contention/locks).

2) Known issue clarity:
- Target: 0 “unknown/untriaged” recurring failure modes at GA; known issues list exists with workaround/ETA.

## Measurement plan (how we will measure the above)
- Operator time and end-to-end time captured during:
  - internal restore drills (SRE-led)
  - 2-customer pilot drills (SE + customer operator)
- Evidence capture uses the standard DR drill template (timeline, commands, outputs, screenshots of dashboard panels).
- Backup success/freshness measured via new metrics emitted by backup jobs and displayed on the Private backup/restore dashboard (last success timestamp, age, duration percentiles, failure reasons).

## Packaging readiness criteria (GA gate)
GA packaging is “complete” when all items below are true for both VPC and on-prem (where applicable):

1) Versioned tooling
- `rw-private-dr` (or equivalent) commands are versioned, documented, and shipped with the redwood-private-installer release artifacts.
- Backward compatibility note: restore tooling version compatibility matrix documented (at minimum: N and N-1 Private releases supported).

2) Kubernetes integration
- Helm charts support:
  - scheduled backup CronJob
  - one-shot restore Job
  - concurrency safeguards (no overlapping backups)
  - configurable windows/timeouts/retries
- Resource requests/limits guidance included.

3) Storage targets
- Supported target(s) clearly labeled as GA vs “best effort”.
- For GA: S3 (incl. MinIO/S3-compatible for on-prem) + at least one filesystem-based option (NFS/mounted repo) for air-gapped workflows.
- Storage target compatibility matrix published.

4) Encryption + key handling defaults
- Encryption in transit and at rest is the default and is verifiable (runbook includes how to confirm).
- Customer-owned keys supported where applicable (KMS/HSM integration pattern documented).

5) Upgrade/rollback integration
- “Backup before upgrade” gate is implemented and documented (what counts as acceptable evidence of backup + verification).

## Documentation readiness criteria (GA gate)
Docs are “GA ready” when:

1) Operator docs complete and navigable
- Overview page defines scope, what is backed up, what is not backed up, terminology, prerequisites.
- Runbooks exist and are internally consistent:
  - Create + verify backup
  - Restore in-place
  - Restore to new cluster
  - DR planning (RPO/RTO tiers + recommended configs)
  - Air-gapped constraints and offline artifact handling

2) Troubleshooting + escalation
- SRE/support troubleshooting guide exists with:
  - alert interpretation
  - log locations
  - known failure modes + fixes
  - escalation criteria to Eng Private

3) Security review readiness
- Key handling guidance published (least privilege, rotation expectations, redaction requirements).
- Evidence checklist published for customer security reviews (what logs/records can be provided, what Redwood does/doesn’t access).

4) Validation gates documented
- Restore validation steps are explicit (health checks, smoke tests, rollback path if validation fails).
- Clear “stop conditions” (when to halt and escalate).

## Pilot exit criteria
We should not declare GA until:
- 2 design partners complete at least one restore drill each (in-place or new-cluster) using GA candidate tooling and runbooks.
- Pilot feedback collected in standard template; all P0 issues resolved, P1 issues have committed workaround + fix ETA.

## GA sign-off (RACI)
- Product (Vivek): metric targets + publishability decision
- Eng Private Deployments (owner TBD in Eng): packaging completeness and release readiness
- SRE (Rafael/Miles/Sean): drill outcomes + observability/alerting readiness
- Security (Marcus/Hanae) + Compliance (Olga): key handling + evidence expectations
- Docs (Elliot/Kira): information architecture + runbook quality
- Solutions (Markus/Fatima): pilot execution confirmation

  - sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/*
  - sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0137-private-backup-format-and-encryption.json
  - sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions/private-backup-key-handling-guidance.json

## Open questions
1) Do we want different GA targets for VPC vs on-prem (given bandwidth constraints), or publish ranges with environment assumptions?
2) What is the minimum supported “strict tier” config for GA (e.g., frequency + retention + replication), and do we ship Terraform examples for it?
3) How do we define/label clusters as “paused” to suppress backup freshness alerts without losing visibility?

## Next steps
- Align on final numeric targets with SRE + Solutions (use pilot environments to validate assumptions).
- Convert targets into a single GA checklist used in release go/no-go.
- Ensure dashboards/alerts expose the required measurements (backup age, success rate, duration, failure reason).
comments: 2025-11-20 — Vivek Kulkarni: Creating this to de-risk GA. Engineering is building the toolkit, but we need measurable criteria for “done” that Support/SRE/Solutions can use without interpretation.

2025-12-03 — Sean Gallagher: +1 on separating operator time vs wall-clock. Customers get upset about on-keyboard complexity even if jobs run quickly. We should explicitly measure both in game days and pilots.

2025-12-09 — Elliot Price: Docs note: we can hit the runbook completeness gate, but we need a single “docs readiness checklist” for reviewers (screenshots, expected outputs, stop conditions). Please include that in GA sign-off.

2025-12-16 — Marcus Lin: Security gate request: GA should require a published key handling FAQ + a clear statement that Redwood never receives plaintext customer KMS/HSM key material. Also need log redaction guidance for backup job env vars/args.

2026-01-08 — Markus Klein: From Solutions perspective, pilot exit criteria must include at least one air-gapped-ish workflow (mounted repo/offline bundle) or we will get surprised in procurement cycles. Suggest: 2 pilots total, but at least 1 with restricted egress.

2026-01-22 — Allison Grant: Observability: we can support backup age, success, duration percentiles, and failure reason breakdown. Need final alert thresholds (warning vs page) and a convention for suppressing alerts on paused clusters.

2026-02-10 — Vivek Kulkarni: Updated targets and added GA sign-off RACI. Pending: confirm numeric RTO/RPO ranges with SRE after next restore drill and incorporate any pilot learnings into the final published guidance.
